title.narrative: Strengthening the capacity of the Republic of Moldova to comply with the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) under the Paris Agreement

description.narrative: E.1 Knowledge management and Communication72. An integrated approach to Knowledge Management and Learning has been developed during Project Preparation and is detailed in the Project Description. Dedicated activities have been budgeted with a clear timeline for delivery, including participation in knowledge exchange through the CBIT Global Coordination Platform. 73. The project adopts a structured Knowledge Management approach to ensure that data, experience, and lessons generated throughout implementation contribute to national, regional, and global learning on climate transparency. These activities are embedded across all project components and aim to enhance institutional memory, inform policy, and support replication of successful practices. 74. Key objectives of the Knowledge Management Plan are: · To document and disseminate good practices and lessons learned from the enhancement of Moldova’s MRV/ETF system, including institutional understanding of how Article 6 mechanisms intersect with Article 13 transparency requirements. · To support institutional learning through workshops, after-action reviews, and knowledge products tailored to different stakeholder groups (e.g., ministries, private sector, academia). · To ensure that knowledge generated is shared with regional partners and global platforms, including the CBIT Global Coordination Platform, to contribute to collective learning on climate transparency. 75. A tailored communication plan will raise awareness of transparency goals and project achievements among key audiences, including national stakeholders, development partners, and the public. Communication tools will include social media campaigns, project newsletters, infographics, and policy dialogues. Special focus will be placed on communicating the role of private sector actors in MRV, highlighting their contributions through case studies and public-private forums. E.2 Socio-economic Benefits and Decent Rural Employment [42] 76. The project will support the strengthening of socio-economic data related to climate change impacts on vulnerable groups, disaggregated by sex, age, and disability. This effort aims to enhance the design and implementation of climate policies and measures that are inclusive and evidence-based. Strengthening this data foundation contributes significantly to improving socio-economic outcomes at both national and local levels, while also aligning with global environmental and adaptation goals. 77. At the national level, the project will enhance Moldova’s institutional and technical capacities for climate change monitoring and reporting. Improved climate data management and transparency will inform policy decisions, enabling more effective mitigation and adaptation strategies. These advances are expected to contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and increasing resilience to climate-related shocks, in line with the objectives of the GEF Trust Fund. 78. At the local level, enhanced capacities of policymakers and stakeholders in rural areas will support the development of strategies that foster full and productive employment and decent work. Strengthening skills and knowledge—particularly in agriculture, forestry, and land-use sectors—will empower communities to adopt sustainable practices that generate stable livelihoods. These outcomes are expected to promote rural economic development, reduce poverty, and support the realization of the right to Decent Rural Employment.79. The project’s emphasis on capacity building, inclusive data systems, and cross-sector collaboration will contribute to Moldova’s broader sustainable development objectives. Supporting a transition toward climate-resilient and low-emission development pathways will deliver long-term socio-economic and environmental benefits that align with both Moldova’s national strategies and global efforts to address climate change. [42] Specific guidance on how FAO can promote the Four Pillars of Decent Work in rural areas is provided in the Quick reference for addressing decent rural employment (as well as in the full corresponding Guidance document). For more information on FAO’s work on decent rural employment and related guidance materials please consult the FAO thematic website at: http://www.fao.org/rural-employment/en/.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To support the Republic of Moldova to meet enhanced transparency framework (ETF) requirements for action and support, as defined in Article 13 of the Paris Agreement, by strengthening institutional and technical capacity for measuring and reporting on emissions (GHG inventory), tracking progress on NDCs, including mitigation and adaptation activities, and finance, technology, development and capacity building support received and needed.
